title: Detecting in-solution conformational changes in viral fusogens using tryptophan-induced fluorescence quenching
protocol: Transform the pET46 Ek/LIC plasmid encoding N-terminal 6xHis-tagged ICV HEF2 into E. coli BL21(DE3) cells.
Plate transformed cells on a LB-agar Amp plate.
Incubate plates at 37°C for at least 12 hours.
Inoculate a single colony in 5 mL LB broth with 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate the inoculated culture at 37°C for 16 h in an Eppendorf Excella E24R orbital shaker at 180 rpm.
Inoculate 1 L of LB broth containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin with 5 mL of the starter culture and incubate at 37°C in an Eppendorf Excella E24R orbital shaker at 180 rpm until O.D.600nm is ∼0.6.
Add IPTG to a final concentration of 0.5 mM to induce protein expression.
Incubate the induced culture at 18°C for 20 h in an Eppendorf I26R orbital shaker at 180 rpm.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 4,000 rpm using a Fiberlite F10S-4x1000 LEX rotor (3,000g) in a Sorvall RC6+ high-capacity centrifuge for 45 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the harvested cells in 30 mL of pre-chilled Buffer A.
Lysate the cells at 30,000 psi using a Constant Systems TS-series 0.75 cell disruption system.
Centrifuge the lysate at 13,500 rpm using a Fiberlite F21-8x50y rotor (21,600g) in a Sorvall RC6+ high-capacity centrifuge for 45 min at 4°C to remove cell debris.
Decant the supernatant.
Filter using a low-protein binding 0.22-μm PES syringe filter.
Pack a 3 mL bed volume of Ni-NTA resin in a 15 x 200 mm gravity flow open column.
Equilibrate the resin with 10 column volumes Buffer A.
Apply the ICV HEF2-containing clarified lysate onto the Ni-NTA column by gravity at 4°C.
Wash the resin with 15 column volumes Buffer B.
Elute ICV HEF2 using 5 column volumes Buffer C.
Add 1 U thrombin per 1 mg protein to the eluate.
Dialyze the thrombin-protein mixture against 1 L Buffer D at 4°C for 16 hours using 12–14 kDa MWCO dialysis tubing.
Lower the concentrations of imidazole by dialysis either before or during thrombin digestion.
Do not use serine protease inhibitors during thrombin digestion.
Concentrate dialyzed ICV HEF2 to 1 mL using an Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal concentrator at a speed of 3,800 rpm at 4°C in a TX-750 rotor.
Inject sample onto a Superdex 75 prep grade resin XK 16/40 gel filtration column pre-equilibrated with Buffer D.
Monitor elution fractions by absorbance at 280 nm.
Pool protein-containing fractions.
Concentrate pooled fractions to ∼1.8 mg/mL using an Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Unit (10 kDa MWCO) at 3,800 rpm in a Sorvall XTR benchtop centrifuge at 4°C.
Quantify protein concentration by determining absorbance at 280 nm on a NanoDrop 2000c or another equivalent spectrophotometer.
Calculate the theoretical molar extinction coefficient from the protein sequence using web servers such as Expasy ProtParam.
Analyze protein purity by 16% SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis.
Stain gel for 10 min with Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250 stain and destain in 10% (v/v) acetic acid.
Aliquot 0.5 ml of 1.8 mg/mL purified ICV HEF2 into pre-chilled 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 55 μl of freshly prepared 100 mM mBBr stock to the purified ICV HEF2 (final concentration 0.5 mM mBBr).
Incubate the sample for 2 h at 22°C in the dark to avoid fluorophore degradation.
Keep the labeling reaction in the dark using aluminum foil.
Examine the protein sample for precipitation before continuing.
Optimize the labeling time and reaction temperature if necessary to prevent protein precipitation.
Use circular dichroism wavelength scans and thermal melts to determine whether protein structure or stability was affected by bimane labeling.
Pre-equilibrate a 5 mL Hi-Trap Desalting column with 20 column volumes of Buffer D.
Remove excess unreacted mBBr using the pre-equilibrated Hi-Trap Desalting column at a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Measure the A280 for each eluted fraction from the desalting column.
Pool the fractions containing the protein based on A280 measurements.
Concentrate the pooled fractions using an Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Unit (10 kDa MWCO) by centrifuging at 3,800 rpm for 3,150g at 4°C.
Pause point: Bimane-labeled ICV HEF2 can be stored in the dark using aluminum foil at 4°C for up to 24 hours without loss of fluorescence signal.
Dilute bimane-labeled ICV HEF2 to 0.5 mg/mL in buffer with desired pH.
Calculate labeling efficiency as a ratio of moles of protein labeled with bimane over moles of unlabeled protein samples.
Measure the UV absorbance at wavelength 295 nm and 390 nm using a NanoDrop 2000c spectrophotometer.
Calculate the labeling efficiency using the provided equation.
Pipette 200 μL of bimane-labelled protein sample at various pH values and associated buffers into a 96-well quartz plate.
Incubate the plate in 2% (v/v) Hellmanex III for 20 min.
Rinse the plate well with doubly distilled H2O.
Dry the plate thoroughly using N2 gas or compressed air before loading each sample.
Measure the fluorescence of bimane-labeled ICV HEF2 using a Synergy Neo2 multimode plate reader or equivalent fluorescence plate reader at 22°C.
Set fluorescence excitation wavelength to 395 (± 5) nm and perform data acquisition in top-to-top mode with autogain.
Collect the emission spectra from 425 to 600 nm with a 1-nm monochromator step and 0.5–1 nm bandwidth, depending on signal intensity.
Set acquisition time to 100 ms and 10 integrations.
Perform an initial measurement using only Buffer D and the sample at pH 7.5 to set autogain function and determine background profile.
Optimize slit and bandwidth for bimane-labeled protein and keep constant for all experiments.
Repeat experiments in triplicates with independently expressed and purified batches of protein.
Measure each data point in technical triplicates.
Measure free mBBr at various pH values as a reference control.
Buffer subtract the acquired technical triplicate data using the reference values obtained from the Buffer D fluorescence scan.
Average the replicates after buffer subtraction.
Normalize the data from 0 to 1.
Average the normalized independent replicates and calculate the standard error of the mean (SEM).
Calculate the quenching factor (F/F0) for each pH.
Perform a one-way ANOVA on the F/F0 quenching fraction to determine statistically significant differences between pH groups.
Perform Tukey’s post-hoc test to determine whether there are statistically different groups.
Estimate the average Cα-Cα distance between the probe and tryptophan residues using the calculated ICV HEF2 quenching fraction (F/F0).
